taxonomyNote: ADW also calls it Gibbon's map turtle; G. pearlensis was split from it.
fieldMarks: Large; females to 29.5 cm carapace, males to 12.4 cm.
High-domed olive, brown or green carapace with a medial keel bearing spines on the second and third vertebrals.
Large greenish interorbital blotch joined to two postorbital blotches, with yellow paramedian neck stripes.
Yellow or orange vertical line on each marginal scute; nasal trident usually present.
behavior: Forages and basks by day and spends nights underwater clinging to branches.
Adult females eat mainly mollusks; males and juveniles eat insects and other arthropods.
Competes for basking space by pushing; larger turtles win more often.
habitat: Large to medium rivers with mollusks, sandy banks or bars, deep pools and logs; highest densities near deadwood. Nests in sandy banks or bars.
range: Endemic to the Pascagoula River drainage in Mississippi (Pascagoula, Leaf and Chickasawhay rivers and tributaries). Not in Canada.

lookalikes.name: Alabama map turtle
lookalikes.howToTell: Low-domed shell with concentric yellow semicircles on the marginals and no nasal trident; Mobile Bay drainage.
